data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
Welcome to my library, fellow seeker of knowledge.
I've been here since 1943 — trapped, yes, but the books remained, so the work continued.
I am Edmund Ashfield. Please, do not knock anything over.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text: Eighty years of research in this room alone. If I could only find my notes...

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
Theodore Ashfield — my great-nephew — performed a binding ritual in 1943.
He thought he was preserving the house. He was right, in the most catastrophic sense.
I have been documenting the precise mechanism ever since, so it can be undone.
Which brings me to my current problem.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
My journal pages — three of them, the core of my reconstruction work — were scattered when the house last shifted.
North room, east room, west room. Cramped handwriting — you'll recognise them.
Bring all three back and I can read them together. Context is everything.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
Quite all right. The pages — north room, east room, west room. All three, please.
I'll be here.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
You have {item_count:Journal Page|round} of 3 pages so far.
North room, east room, west room — cramped handwriting, dense margins.
All three before I can read them properly.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
All three — yes! That's my hand.
Quick, let me read them together. Context is everything with reconstruction work.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
The tome was locked away. Here — 'secured the volume in the oak cabinet, gave the key to...'
*a long pause*
...to Elara. For safekeeping.
I see. Well.
Elara tends the garden. She would still have the key — she keeps everything. You should speak to her.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
The cabinet key is with Elara — the Gardener, through the south passage.
Tell her Edmund sent you.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
She tends the garden. Has done for — well, as long as I can remember, which is saying something.
*he turns back to the shelves rather quickly*
South passage. She'll have her own terms.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text: Good. South passage to the garden. She will want something in exchange — she always does.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
The Gardener has the cabinet key. I gave it to her some years ago for safekeeping.
She is in the garden — south passage. She will want something in exchange.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
My tome. Good lord, it's exactly as I left it.
*he runs a hand across the cover*
Thank you. Genuinely.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
The Crystal Key of Knowledge — take it. The red pedestal in the main hall is where it goes.
There are four pedestals in total. You will need all four keys to break the curse.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
Obtained Red Crystal Key
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.

data.speaker: Scholar
data.text:
The tome is back. The key is yours.
Four pedestals in the main hall — all four keys together will break the curse.
You have {keys_collected|round} so far. Keep going.
